Gamma ratio asymptotics give the uniform row summand Gamma(alpha+4+epsilon)Gamma(-alpha)n^(-1-epsilon)+O(n^(-2-epsilon)). Summing n up to N with epsilon=lambda/logN yields logN*Phi(lambda)+O(1), uniformly for bounded signed lambda. The truncated column k>N tail is O(1) because alpha<0; this handles the noncompact half of the compression. The two-dimensional limiting measure is obtained by k/n Riemann sums of x^(alpha+1)/(1+x)^2 and logarithmic n-sums; small/large x and near-end t tails control extension to all bounded continuous tests. The same row estimate summed to infinity with epsilon>0 gives 1/epsilon+O(1). Independent finite alpha=-1/2 computations at N=90,240,600 are consistent with an O(1) cutoff correction but cannot prove any limit.
